what_happened: Validated Item 6(b)'s reuse design (write-time cycle refusal by shelling out to validate-state.sh --deep against a scratch state.json copy, grepping its exact FAIL line) by running it against two synthetic fixtures (cyclic and acyclic); confirmed it works without any edit to validate-state.sh, which matters because that file is outside this task's declared file_scope.

Falsified a tempting numeric default for Item 6(a)'s dependency-edge direction rule (e.g. higher task-number depends on lower) using this task's own live dependency graph: tasks 274 and 312, both lower-numbered/older than 344, each carry a dependency edge ONTO 344 (the newer task), because 344 is their real prerequisite. Direction must be fixed by call-argument shape, not inferred from task numbering.

Planning-time measurement found the eager-context budget has only 9 bytes of headroom (live TOTAL 65941 B vs orchestrator-context-budget.json eager_load.baseline_bytes 65950 B), and verify-deploy.sh Gate 20 sub-check B fail()s on any regression above baseline. Item 1's addition to merge-sources/claudemd.md (an eager-loaded file) therefore CANNOT be a net add; it must be byte-neutral via an offsetting in-file trim, and orchestrator-context-budget.json is not in this task's file_scope so the baseline cannot be moved. Research justified the token cost in the abstract but did not check this hard ceiling.

Grounded every phase's Verification Tier mechanically instead of guessing, by sourcing scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh and running suite_selection_select against all five declared file_scope paths. Two paths (multi-task-operations.md, merge-sources/claudemd.md) return the __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel, so their Tier Justifications name --only-gate 3,4 honestly rather than claiming a covering suite; batch-orchestration-guardrails.md resolves to three real suites and update-task-status.sh plus its test resolve to the suite being extended, so those justifications name run-all.sh --only with the exact resolved basenames.

Editing batch-orchestration-guardrails.md (in file_scope) changed its line count, which required a mechanical generate-context-line-counts.sh --write regeneration touching agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json (not declared in file_scope). Included in the Phase 1 commit as a necessary, directly-caused side effect of an in-scope edit; no unrelated content changed.
